_comment: USGS SJWSE_111_1424 single baseline N141 (base) -> M141/973159 (rover), 2025 DOY 111.
Requested by the gnss-qc-lite session.  Short baseline ~1.35 km, RINEX 3.05 MIXED, 1 s.
SETUP DECISIONS (all reported back with the result):
- GPS ONLY.  Both files carry GLONASS, but the two receivers are DIFFERENT types
(base IGAIG9 / CHC, rover CHC 1915) with 'Unknown' antennas, so the GLONASS
inter-frequency phase bias does NOT cancel in the double difference and would
corrupt the integer fix rather than strengthen it.  A GPS+GLONASS arm is run
separately as _usgs_n141_m141_gr.json for comparison only.
- 30 s decimation (processing.gnss_rate_s) from the native 1 s.  A static 1.35 km
baseline is fully determined at 30 s; 1 s would be 43200 epochs for no gain.
- RECEIVER PCO/PCV OFF.  Both headers declare ANT # / TYPE 'Unknown', so there is
no IGS antenna model to key off.  The two antenna heights DO differ (2.0750 m
base vs 2.0000 m rover), so the ARP offsets still apply; what is missing is the
phase-centre model.  This is the vertical-component caveat.
- SATELLITE PCO/PCV ON (igs20.atx resolves from data/static/atx).  Over 1.35 km
the satellite-side terms cancel in DD anyway.
- OCEAN TIDE LOADING OFF: EOT20_load.nc is not in the internal data tree, and the
DIFFERENTIAL ocean loading over 1.35 km is far below a millimetre.  Solid-earth
and pole tide stay on (no external file needed) and likewise cancel.
- SUPERSEDED (see REVISION): broadcast nav alone does NOT drive geometry.
- SUPERSEDED (see REVISION): broadcast nav alone does NOT drive geometry.
REVISION (verified against the NGS datasheets, sub-mm reproduction):
(E -4.64 N +7.17 U +5.59).  The VECTOR is insensitive either way
(1352 x 10 / 20.2e6 = 0.7 mm), but holding the published value puts the
solution in NAD 83(2011) so the solved ROVER position is directly
comparable to HN0157's published coordinate.
- Precise products REQUIRED: baseline mode fills its orbit cache from SP3
only (ProductParser::loadProducts -> parseSp3); the RNX broadcast path
feeds Klobuchar coefficients ALONE, so broadcast-only cannot drive
geometry despite the comment at ApplicationBaseline.cpp:113.
- TRUTH for grading, ARP-to-ARP, published-derived and independently
NOTE U != dh: dh(ARP) = 21.4830 m and U = 21.3394 m differ by the
curvature term s^2/2R = 0.1435 m.  Grade against U, not dh.
- ⚠ CONVENTION: config-supplied position_ecef is consumed AT FACE VALUE as the
ANTENNA (ARP) position — ApplicationBaseline.cpp:173 takes reference.position_ecef
verbatim, and the rover comment at :350-353 states it: 'a config-supplied
coordinate is taken at face value (the user owns its reference point)'.  Only the
RINEX-HEADER fallback reduces marker -> ARP (getArpPositionXyz).  So the published
datasheet coordinate, which is the MARK/monument, MUST be pre-reduced here.
Base  = HN0156 mark + 2.0750 m along its own up vector.
Rover = HN0157 mark + 2.0000 m along its own up vector (a-priori only; estimated).
Failing to pre-reduce would have put a 2.075 m error on the base and made the
solved vector match NEITHER truth row.
- GRADE AGAINST THE ARP-to-ARP ROW (both endpoints are ARP by the above):
The MARK-to-MARK row differs ONLY in Up, by exactly the 0.0750 m antenna-height
difference (U +21.4144); horizontal agrees to <0.5 mm.  Grading against the wrong
row manufactures a 75 mm vertical bias, 3x the 24 mm realization floor.
To compare the solved ROVER position to HN0157's published MARK, subtract
2.0000 m along the rover's up vector first.
- ⚠ processing.gnss_rate_s is INERT in baseline mode: it is applied only in
Application::run (Application.cpp:1723); neither ApplicationBaseline.cpp nor
MultiRinexSync references it.  The observation files are therefore PRE-DECIMATED
to 30 s with scripts/decimate_rinex3_obs.py; the knob is left in place only as
documentation of intent.
